newsitem.title: UK: LME technical rallies falter, markets close mixed.
newsitem.headline: LME technical rallies falter, markets close mixed.

text.p: Technical rallies in the LME base metal complex ran out of steam during late Thursday trading, and contracts finished mixed.

Analysts said that the initial rallies, which were led by copper, reflected the sell-offs seen this week attracting some Far Eastern buying interest, which then trigered short-covereing. But business was not particularly active.
"I would have been surprised if there had not been a correction after yesterday (in copper), but the bears are still in the driving seat," said Angus MacMillan of LME trader Billiton Metals.

Traders said levels of $2,230 on Wednesday - a 4-1/2 month low - were the springboard for a technical correction. But the rally faded, as expected, near $2,295/2,300. Last trade was at $2,268, still up $32 from Wednesday's kerb.
"It was a bit of a jobbing market today, with the dealers looking to sell the rallies eventually," one trader said.
The spreads largely held around yesterday's levels, with cash/threes at a $110/120 backwardation. July tightness remains paramount, with "third Wednesday" pricing next Monday.
Aluminium tended to mirror copper, and was unable to wade through the resistance above $1,580. By the kerb prices were just $2 higher at $1,570.

May IPAI producer inventory data was mixed, with total stocks down, but unwrought up, and thus had little impact on sentiment. Another one-day strike at Spanish producer Inespal also had little affect, traders said.
Nickel again fell back during the afternoon sessions, having encountered overhead resistance above $6,900.
Also, stocks are seen rising in coming weeks, despite today's decrease, given talk of ample Russian availability. Last trade was at $6,850, down $40.
Zinc eased back from the resistance above $1,480, but still ended higher, reflecting the narrowing contango and increasing tightness in September.
Last three months business was at $1,479, a $15 gain from Wednesday, with the market expected to re-test last week's 6-3/4 year highs of $1,495 soon.
The cash/threes contango was $8/10 at the close, while September/threes months was at an $11 backwardation.
Lead also settled back from its peaks, but similarly remained higher, building on morning gains and expectations of improving fundamentals as the battery season nears.
"As we move into the third quarter it is looking quite promising. The stocks are less than five weeks consumption," MacMillan said.
Prices ended at $660, up $10 from the previous kerb, with the market targeting $675.
Tin was quiet throughout the session, and struggled to make much of an upside impression. Three months closed at $5,520, up just $10.
Alloy was quoted at a steadier $1,425/35 a tonne.
